title: Jobs must omit permissions to inherit an empty token; job-level permissions: {} is denied
answers: can a GitHub Actions job set permissions: {}
conftest says job is redundant permissions {}
how do I give a workflow job no GITHUB_TOKEN permissions
job missing permissions policy error in workflow
body:
Invariant: a workflow job must not set job-level `permissions: {}`. A job that needs no token either omits `permissions` (inheriting the workflow-level default) or declares a non-empty grant.
Enforced by .github/policy.rego:deny_redundant_job_permissions, which denies any job whose `permissions` equals `{}` and names the job in the message ("Omit it to inherit the workflow's empty default permissions").
The older requirement that every job declare `permissions` (deny_jobs_without_permissions, with its helper jobs_without_permissions) was removed; do not reintroduce it, because omitting permissions is now the accepted way to get an empty token.
Fix pattern: when a job needs no token scopes, delete its `permissions: {}` line and rely on the workflow-level `permissions: {}`. This PR removed four such lines in copilot-agent.yml, rerun.yml, ui-preview.yml and ui-review.yml.
Constraints: omitting is only an empty grant when the workflow-level `permissions` is `{}`; the rule checks only the job-level value and does not verify the workflow default. Non-empty grants must still be declared explicitly on the job.
applies: Jobs under `jobs:` in .github/workflows/*.yml; the job-level rule does not cover composite action.yml files.
says: Automated compliance check fails on pipeline jobs that request empty access permissions.
The pull request policy check rejects pipeline tasks configured with blank permissions.
Allow automated build jobs without special access rights to pass security compliance checks.
Workflow validation blocks pull requests claiming job permissions should be omitted instead.
Strip unnecessary permission blocks from automated workflow steps so pull requests pass.
search: Workflow jobs must not set job-level permissions: {} and must instead omit permissions to inherit empty workflow defaults or declare non-empty grants. This is enforced under jobs: in .github/workflows/*.yml by .github/policy.rego:deny_redundant_job_permissions, while deny_jobs_without_permissions was removed and must not be reintroduced. To fix violations, delete the permissions: {} line from the job, noting that omission only yields an empty grant if workflow-level permissions is {} and composite action.yml files are not covered.
